assertions.name: k2_pole_lattice_map_exact_and_uniquely_selective
assertions.source: q = 1.2, sympy exact + 60 dps: for an input with a Borel-plane pole at xi* = 1/sqrt(2) (model), the atomic-kernel q-Laplace output's pole set is EXACTLY xi*(1-p)/u · qt^Z (identity xi*/t = xi*(1-p)/u·qt^(2m-j) exact; exponent set j-2m covers Z; all masses positive so residues cannot cancel; every computed pole lands on the lattice, rel < 1e-30, for u = 1, 1.3, qt^(1/2)). The map u |-> [lattice class] is a FREE TRANSITIVE circle action (class shift = -log_qt u exactly), so ONE known output pole location selects a UNIQUE u mod qt^Z: the solved u places a pole on x_tgt = 0.53 to < 1e-30 while a qt^0.37-detuned u misses by 0.37 of a step. KSel-1 is well-formed and uniquely selective IN FORM — given an input-side singularity and an output-side datum

assertions.name: k4_output_positive_axis_u_invariant
assertions.source: q = 1.2, 60 dps, truncation N = 30, x = 0.3: the atomic-kernel double sum sum_a c_a·fhat_N(x t_a)/t_a equals the u-INDEPENDENT truncated balanced series sum b^q_n·N^bal(n)·x^n to rel < 1e-25 for u = 1, 1.3, and qt^(1/2) (extends the REP R3 falsifier per-u). Since every term is positive for x > 0, Tonelli rearrangement makes this exact at the function level: the kernel output on the positive real axis IS the u-independent series wherever it converges and +inf beyond r* — for EVERY u. The positive-axis output singularity x* = r* (K3b) is therefore EXACTLY u-invariant, by the same reindex mechanism that makes the moments u-invariant

assertions.name: k4_ksel1_verdict_continuum_survives
assertions.source: VERDICT (scope-(a)): the u-translate CONTINUUM SURVIVES KSel-1 (singularity matching). The principle is well-formed and uniquely selective in form (K2: an input Borel-plane pole + one output pole datum pin a unique u mod qt^Z, free transitive circle action), but the QOU binding data fail both hypotheses: (input) the fibre q-Borel-side carrier is ENTIRE — b^q_n ~ q^(-n^2/4)·rho_phi^(-n), no finite singularity to match (K3a, both q0 pins); (output) the only corpus-computable output singularity — the positive-axis wall at x* = r* ~ 0.34042 (q0), newly measured in K3b — is EXACTLY u-invariant by Tonelli + moment u-invariance (K4); and the only independently-known corpus singularity datum (xi = 1/sqrt(2)) lives at q = 1 in the classical level-1/2 plane, where the kernel class is already the Carleman singleton and u is not a parameter (K1 tier table). No unique u is selected; no fit; nothing wired; the (REP) canonical-choice premise stays open. A future selection would need an OFF-positive-axis output datum (e.g. the negative-axis / complex pole lattice of the analytic continuation past r*, which IS u-dependent per K2's mechanism) — not currently in the corpus

assertions.name: k5_selfdual_moments_circle_and_halfstep
assertions.source: q = 1.2, 60 dps: (i) the full kernel's ds/s-moments equal N^bal at u = 1, 1.3, AND the sigma-self-dual point u = qt^(1/2) (rel < 1e-30 — u-invariance holds at the KSel-3 maximal-symmetry candidates, as forced by the REP R4a reindex identity); (ii) the family is a genuine circle: mu_(qt·u) = mu_u as normalized measures (< 1e-25); (iii) sigma: s -> qt^(-1)/s maps mu_u -> mu_(1/u) and fixes exactly the classes u = 1 and u = qt^(1/2) (measure equalities < 1e-25); (iv) the two self-dual points' model pole-lattice classes differ by exactly HALF a qt-step (|frac - 1/2| < 1e-25). RECORDED, NOT INTERPRETED: KSel-1 selects no u (K4), so no selected-u-vs-self-dual coincidence exists to evaluate; the half-step offset is the exact discriminant a future measured output pole lattice would use to split the two KSel-3 symmetry-maximal candidates

description: KSel-1 (singularity matching) on the (REP) canonical-choice continuum (bean qou-334t; audit-only, scope-(a), NO FIT, nothing wired; machinery reused with attribution from rep_jackson_identification_probe / bean qou-u5p0). K1: the corpus's independently-known binding Borel singularity datum re-pinned with tiers — q = 1 level-1/2 plane, xi* = 1/sqrt(2) on the positive real axis (Pringsheim exact; class Lean-proved Gevrey-1/2; location measured scope-(a)); at q0 the corpus already showed that classical plane collapses. K2 (model leg): the exact map u |-> output pole set derived and verified — an input Borel-plane pole at xi* puts the atomic-kernel q-Laplace output's poles EXACTLY on xi*(1-p)/u·qt^Z (positivity forbids residue cancellation); u |-> [lattice class] is a free transitive circle action, so one output-pole datum would select a UNIQUE u mod qt^Z: KSel-1 is uniquely selective IN FORM. K3 (q = 1.2 + both q0 pins, n <= 400): the REAL binding data fail both hypotheses — the q-Borel-side carrier b^q_n = S(n)/[n]_q! satisfies b^q_n ~ q^(-n^2/4)·rho_phi^(-n) (two-cycle-converged), so phi is ENTIRE (no input singularity to match); the balanced period series is GEOMETRIC with newly measured radius r* (~0.46807 at q = 1.2; ~0.34039 at both q0 pins), all coefficients positive => the output-side singularity is the positive-axis wall x* = r*. K4: by Tonelli (positivity) + moment u-invariance the kernel output on the positive axis IS the u-independent series for EVERY u (verified < 1e-25 at u = 1, 1.3, qt^(1/2)) — the wall x* = r* is EXACTLY u-invariant. VERDICT: the u-continuum SURVIVES KSel-1 — no unique u; the selection axis is degenerate on the positive axis for the same reindex reason the moments are u-invariant, and has no input-side referent (phi entire). K5: balanced moments hold at the sigma-self-dual points u = 1 and u = qt^(1/2) (u-invariance asserted); the family is a circle (mu_(qt·u) = mu_u); the two self-dual points' model pole-lattice classes differ by exactly half a qt-step — recorded, not interpreted (no selected u exists for a KSel-3 coincidence). Nothing here proves or refutes the conjecture.
